explanations.tree/all_mastered: A tree is a hierarchical data structure where each node connects to zero or more child nodes. Since you know recursion, you can traverse trees by recursively visiting each node's children.
explanations.tree/missing_prereq: A tree is a hierarchical data structure where each node connects to zero or more child nodes. You can traverse trees using recursion because each subtree mirrors the entire tree's recursive pattern.
explanations.tree/several_low: A tree is a hierarchical structure where each node connects to zero or more child nodes. You can traverse it using recursion because each subtree follows the same pattern as the whole tree.
explanations.tree/uncertain: A tree is a hierarchical data structure where each node connects to zero or more child nodes. Since you know recursion, you can traverse trees by recursively visiting each node's children.
explanations.binary_tree/all_mastered: A binary tree is a type of tree where each node can have up to two children. This structure builds on your understanding of trees and recursion by limiting branching to at most two paths per node.
explanations.binary_tree/missing_prereq: A binary tree is a type of tree where each node can have up to two children. Since you know recursion, this structure naturally supports recursive algorithms for traversing and manipulating trees.
explanations.binary_tree/several_low: A binary tree is a type of tree where each node can have up to two children. This structure helps build recursive algorithms by breaking problems into smaller subproblems.
explanations.binary_tree/uncertain: A binary tree is a type of tree where each node can have up to two children. This structure builds on your understanding of trees and recursion by limiting branching to at most two paths per node.
explanations.heap/all_mastered: A heap is a complete binary tree where each parent node is larger (max-heap) or smaller (min-heap) than its children. It can be efficiently stored in an array while maintaining these properties for fast access and operations.
explanations.heap/missing_prereq: A heap is a complete binary tree where each parent node is larger (or smaller) than its children, and it can be efficiently stored in an array using the parent-child relationships.
explanations.heap/several_low: A heap is a complete binary tree where each parent node is larger (max-heap) or smaller (min-heap) than its children. It can be efficiently stored in an array by placing nodes level by level.
explanations.heap/uncertain: A heap is a complete binary tree where each parent node is larger (max-heap) or smaller (min-heap) than its children. It can be efficiently stored in an array using level-order traversal.
